sources.title: Layers of Deprivation: Multidimensional Poverty in Myanmar
sources.temporal_coverage: People's Pulse Survey 2025; report issued October 2026; shock recall covers the preceding 12 months.
sources.methodology: Nationwide phone survey of 7,463 households; adapted MPI and survey-weighted shock analysis.
sources.limitations: Phone sampling under-represents remote, conflict-affected, stateless and displaced people; shock reports may overlap; associations are not causal.

sources.title: Myanmar: Emergency and Resilience Plan, 2026–2028
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
geographic_coverage: 11 states and regions (not individually named in cited passages)
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026–2028 plan; includes impacts of September 2024 floods and the March 2025 earthquake and describes ongoing FAO field presence.
sources.methodology: FAO strategy drawing on food-security severity analysis, assessments, monitoring and existing field projects.
sources.limitations: Strategic plan, not an independent evaluation; planned activities are commitments, and cited passages provide little named subnational outcome evidence.

sources.title: Myanmar Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2026
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), Myanmar
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026 humanitarian planning period; issued December 2025; draws on 2025 assessments and monitoring.
sources.methodology: Inter-agency plan using multisource needs assessments, partner monitoring and an October 2025 access-severity exercise across 330 townships.
sources.limitations: Planning forecasts are not impact evaluations; data and response reach are constrained by inaccessible areas and reliance on partner reporting.

sources.title: Myanmar Health Cluster Bulletin: August 2026
sources.organization: World Health Organization (WHO) / Myanmar Health Cluster
sources.temporal_coverage: August 2026 disease and flood reporting; health-service figures cover January–June 2026.
sources.methodology: Health Cluster partner reporting on outbreaks, flood impacts and service delivery; 49 partners submitted service data.
sources.limitations: Reporting was incomplete or delayed; medicine and diagnostic shortages constrained response and partner data do not cover all activity.

sources.title: Rakhine State, Western Myanmar: Flood Situation Update No. 1
sources.organization: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), Myanmar
sources.temporal_coverage: Heavy-rain and flood impacts from early July 2026; partner information compiled through 17 July; report cover dated 20 July.
sources.methodology: OCHA compilation of humanitarian-partner flood, damage, needs and response information at township, village and ward levels.
sources.limitations: Affected-population and damage estimates required continued verification; road, communications and access constraints limited assessment and response.

claims.locator: PDF p.26 (printed p.24), §3.2, Figure 5 and note 12.
claims.paraphrase: PPS 2025 respondents reported natural-hazard exposure for 23% of rural versus 10% of urban households; rates were highest in Kayah (52%), Bago (32%), Kayin and Magway (30%), and lowest in Tanintharyi (4%) and Yangon (7%).
claims.limitations: Self-reported, combined hazard category; it is not hazard-specific or climate-attribution evidence.

claims.paraphrase: Survey-adjusted models associate natural-hazard exposure with a 3.8-point increase in predicted MPI poverty (31.3% to 35.0%); conflict exposure had a larger 14.2-point increase (30.6% to 44.8%).
claims.limitations: Model associations, not causal effects; self-reported shock categories may overlap.

claims.locator: PDF p.26 (printed p.24), §3.2; PDF p.28 (printed p.26), cumulative shock analysis.
claims.paraphrase: UNDP reports that natural-hazard, economic and conflict shocks often co-occur; modeled poverty rises with cumulative shocks as assets, savings and household buffers are depleted.
claims.limitations: Aggregate self-reported shocks; the model does not estimate climate-driven conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Natural-hazard and conflict pressures co-occur; cumulative shocks erode household coping capacity.

claims.paraphrase: FAO reports that the September 2024 floods and March 2025 earthquake damaged crops, livestock, inputs and incomes; repeated extreme-weather impacts compound vulnerability and food insecurity in conflict-affected, economically isolated areas.
claims.limitations: FAO synthesizes damage and vulnerability; the passage does not estimate an isolated causal effect.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Climate shocks compound conflict and economic-isolation vulnerabilities, raising food-insecurity and asset-depletion risk.

claims.paraphrase: FAO says many rural households depend on one income source, such as small-scale fishing or monocropping; coastal fishers have few alternatives, and limited diversification heightens shock exposure and asset-depleting coping.
claims.limitations: Broad livelihood categories; the cited section does not name specific communities.

claims.paraphrase: FAO reports field projects in 11 states/regions and its 2026–2028 plan commits to climate-resilient production, flood/drought early warning, local finance and conflict-sensitive natural-resource management.
geographies: 11 states and regions (not individually named in cited passages)
claims.limitations: Field presence is FAO-reported; 2026–2028 activities are commitments, not measured outcomes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: FAO describes these resilience actions as support for conflict-affected rural populations.

claims.locator: PDF p.12, Humanitarian outlook and risks.
claims.paraphrase: For its 2026 planning period, OCHA expects worsening climate disasters and epidemics to erode resilience; northern Rakhine is identified as a food-insecurity and malnutrition hotspot under combined monsoon, conflict and economic pressures.
claims.scenario: 2026 humanitarian planning period; no emissions or climate-model scenario stated.
claims.limitations: Planning forecast rather than a quantified climate scenario or measured causal effect.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Conflict, economic crisis and monsoon floods jointly raise acute food-insecurity and malnutrition risk.

claims.locator: PDF p.22, access-severity exercise (October 2025); PDF p.24, locally-led response.
claims.paraphrase: OCHA found extreme access difficulties in 127 of 330 townships; nearly 95% clustered in conflict-affected northeast, northwest, Rakhine and southeast, where local organizations remain a response backbone.
affected_groups: people in need in hard-to-reach areas
claims.limitations: Access classification and partner reach do not measure assistance quality or household-level outcomes.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Armed conflict, checkpoints and administrative barriers restrict humanitarian movement and reach.

claims.locator: PDF p.1, Highlights; PDF p.2, Public Health Emergencies.
claims.paraphrase: The August bulletin reports monsoon flooding affecting over 470,000 people in Sagaing, Mandalay, Magway, Ayeyarwady and Mon; overflowed latrines contaminated water and food, with AWD cases in Shwebo, Lemyethna, Mandalay and Bago.
claims.limitations: Partner-reported figures; the report notes delayed and incomplete data.

claims.locator: PDF p.2, Sittwe Cholera/AWD outbreak passage.
claims.paraphrase: By 22 August, Sittwe had over 150 Cholera/AWD cases, almost half severe; all were reported in IDP sites, where overcrowding and poor water quality were identified as outbreak drivers.
institutions: Camp Coordination and Camp Management Cluster
claims.limitations: Operational report identifies outbreak conditions but does not isolate causes or report all unrecorded cases.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Report links displacement-site overcrowding and poor water to recurrent outbreak risk.

claims.locator: PDF p.1, Yangon MRCS response; PDF p.2, preparedness and EWARS.
claims.paraphrase: WHO reports MRCS water chlorination, awareness and early detection in Yangon alongside a sharp case decline; shared risk indexing, prepositioned supplies and EWARS supported faster alert verification and response.
claims.limitations: WHO describes response actions and temporal improvement, not a causal evaluation of their effects.

claims.locator: PDF p.1, Highlights and Situation Overview.
claims.paraphrase: Early-July heavy rain and rising rivers flooded 18 wards and 201 villages in Rakhine, affecting 98,282 people; Buthidaung, Kyauktaw, Minbya, Mrauk-U and Ponnagyun were among the hardest-hit townships.
claims.limitations: Partner estimates compiled through 17 July; further verification was required.

claims.locator: PDF p.2, Humanitarian Needs, Access and Operational Constraints, and Response.
claims.paraphrase: Flood-damaged roads and communications, transport disruption, limited stocks and incomplete assessments delayed aid; partners had started WASH, mobile health and cash assistance, but response remained below assessed needs.
claims.limitations: The report attributes delays to physical/logistical constraints, not specifically to armed conflict.

search_audit.query: site:myanmar.un.org/en "Humanitarian Update" Myanmar 2026 flood OCHA October 2026
search_audit.outcome: Opened UNDP's 2026 household survey, OCHA's Rakhine flood update and WHO's Health Cluster bulletin; evidence names states, townships, villages and IDP sites. Kept self-report and partner-estimate limitations.

search_audit.query: Myanmar climate conflict local water livelihood insecurity resource competition UNDP 2025 2026 report subnational
search_audit.outcome: UNDP and FAO directly describe combined hazard/conflict pressures through poverty, food insecurity, assets and household coping; neither estimates climate-caused violence, so no such link is asserted.

search_audit.query: Myanmar 2026 conflict access restrictions humanitarian aid reach climate hazards disasters reverse effect monsoon flooding primary UN report local response
search_audit.outcome: The full HNRP documents conflict/checkpoint/administrative access barriers and local delivery in hard-to-reach areas. The OCHA July access snapshot's official URL returned 403; proxy text was excluded. Rakhine's flood update describes logistical access constraints without attributing them to conflict.

search_audit.query: Myanmar 2026 monsoon flood local response resilience community partners water sanitation WHO report
search_audit.outcome: FAO's plan commits to early warning, resilient agriculture and conflict-sensitive resource management; WHO reports MRCS chlorination and outbreak monitoring; HNRP describes local actors' role in hard-to-reach areas. Commitments are not treated as evaluated outcomes.

gaps: No inspected public source estimated localized climate-related conflict incidence independently of conflict, economic and household vulnerability factors; available links concern food insecurity and coping, not climate-driven violence.
UNDP's 2025 phone survey under-represents remote, conflict-affected, stateless and displaced households; its Rakhine deprivation estimates may understate need.
The official OCHA July 2026 Humanitarian Access Snapshot could not be opened (HTTP 403); search-proxy text was excluded from evidence.
FAO's 2026–2028 resilience measures are commitments, not evaluated outcomes; its cited passages do not identify the 11 states/regions or report comparative local results.
OCHA's Rakhine flood update records physical and logistical access constraints but does not attribute them to armed conflict; no FCV linkage is inferred from this report.
